# Entity Field Coverage

Proof that every field of every entity of the six services was considered. The list is built from the **entity classes** (Java field and type) joined with the **live schema and the seeded rows** (SQL type, nullability, how many rows populate the column), so nothing is documented from memory. 39 tables, 392 columns; only 5 columns are entirely NULL, each for the reason given.

How to read the last column:

* **Generated by JPA/Hibernate** - the application generates the value (random UUID primary keys, or the `@MapsId` shared key); the seed lets the same mechanism run, it never invents an id.
* **Generated by PostgreSQL (IDENTITY)** - `Long` identity keys; rows are inserted without an id and found again by business key.
* **Calculated by the application formula** - money, tax, stock, points and numbers the services compute; the seed reproduces the formula (see ORDERS.md, FINANCE.md, PRODUCTS_AND_TAX.md), it never types a contradicting value.
* **Resolved by business key** - a reference to another service's row (a scalar id with no foreign key); found by email, name, SKU, registration number or order number.
* **Seeded** - a realistic value from the dataset; **Optional** - NULL where the lifecycle stage does not apply (the reason is stated); **NULL by design** - NULL in every row, with the reason.

Populated = rows with a value / rows in the table. "Required" is the database constraint (`NOT NULL`); the Bean Validation rules of the request DTOs (SKU pattern, description length, password policy, 10-digit phones, 6-digit postal codes ...) are honoured by the seed values and asserted in `VALIDATE_SEED_DATA.sql`.

## Enum and status values used

Values come from the source; nothing is invented. Enum columns (Java enums) and status columns (plain strings whose values are fixed by the service code) are listed with the values the seed uses.

| Service | Field | Allowed values in the code | Used by the seed |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | user_account.role | SUPER_ADMIN, OPERATIONS_MANAGER, LOCATION_MANAGER, RETAILER, FLEET_MANAGER, DRIVER, CUSTOMER, SUPPORT_STAFF | all eight |
| S1 | user_account.account_status | ACTIVE, INACTIVE, SUSPENDED, PENDING_VERIFICATION | ACTIVE |
| S1 | operations_manager.assignment_status / location_manager.assignment_status (`AssignmentStatus`) | ACTIVE, INACTIVE, SUSPENDED, TRANSFERRED | ACTIVE |
| S2 | retailer.retailer_status | PENDING, VERIFIED, REJECTED, SUSPENDED | VERIFIED |
| S2 | fleet_owner.profile_status / owner_status | PENDING, VERIFIED, REJECTED, SUSPENDED / PENDING, ACTIVE, INACTIVE | VERIFIED / ACTIVE |
| S2 | verification_queue.subject_type | RETAILER, FLEET_OWNER, DRIVER, VEHICLE | all four |
| S2 | verification_queue.verification_status | DOCUMENTS_SUBMITTED, SENT_TO_LOCATION_MANAGER, RESUBMISSION_REQUIRED, APPROVED, REJECTED | APPROVED |
| S2 | verification_document.document_type_name | GST_CERTIFICATE, PAN_CARD, BUSINESS_LICENSE, ADDRESS_PROOF, GST_NUMBER, DRIVING_LICENSE, INSURANCE | all seven |
| S2 | verification_document.document_status | PENDING, APPROVED, REJECTED | APPROVED, REJECTED (superseded version) |
| S3 | product_categories.status (`CategoryStatus`) | ACTIVE, INACTIVE | ACTIVE (8), INACTIVE (1) |
| S3 | products.status (`ProductStatus`) | ACTIVE, DRAFT | ACTIVE (29), DRAFT (1) |
| S3 | products.quality_flag | TRENDING, LOW_RATED (or NULL) | TRENDING (1) |
| S3 | customer_address.address_tag | HOME, WORK, OTHER | HOME, WORK, OTHER |

| S4 | orders.order_status | NEW, WAITING_FOR_RETAILER, RETAILER_ACCEPTED, RETAILER_REJECTED, FINDING_DELIVERY_PARTNER, BOOKING_CONFIRMED, VEHICLE_ASSIGNED, IN_TRANSIT, DELIVERED, CANCELLED, SHOP_UNAVAILABLE | DELIVERED, IN_TRANSIT, FINDING_DELIVERY_PARTNER, VEHICLE_ASSIGNED, RETAILER_REJECTED, CANCELLED, BOOKING_CONFIRMED |

## Not seeded, on purpose

* `password_reset_token` (S1): a 30-minute secret created by the forgot-password flow; a seeded one would only be an expired row. Its columns are documented above with 0 rows.
* No tables were skipped otherwise: all 39 entity tables carry data, and there is no separate inventory, order-history, brand, MRP, insurance or tax-category table in the current model (stock lives on `products`; order history is the `status_history_json` column and `trip_status_history`; tax is `tax_configuration` keyed by category id).
